title: Borrowed Model Fields Propagating Unnecessary Lifetime Coupling
pattern: Stored borrows (`&'a str`, `&'a [u8]`, `&'a T`) propagate through model hierarchies despite a need for independent ownership or lifetimes, or an unmeasured zero-copy choice introduces widespread lifetime parameters without a demonstrated benefit.
why_bad: Borrowing ties model validity to the source data and can complicate composition, storage, and background work. Avoiding a small copy can impose more architectural complexity than the relevant workload justifies; the time spent fighting lifetime errors far exceeds the negligible cost of cloning a small string.
detection: Trace short-lived reference fields through enclosing structs and APIs. Establish either (a) a struct hierarchy where multiple layers carry a lifetime parameter matching the innermost reference, with concrete composition/storage/lifetime constraints inconsistent with intended use (e.g. the model must outlive its input, be sent to another thread, or be stored long-term); or (b) extensive lifetime propagation adopted to avoid copies in otherwise owning textual/data models (entities holding names or reference strings) without evidence that the tradeoff is worthwhile. An annotation count alone is not sufficient.
source: Jon Gjengset, *Rust for Rustaceans* (2021), Chapter 1 ("Lifetimes"); *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Chapter 20 (p. 319); *Software Design for Flexibility*, Chapter 1 (p. 100); *Refactoring to Patterns*, Chapter 1 (p. 235).
